speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long you have noticed the swelling in your neck and whether it has been growing rapidly or slowly?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of colon cancer, it is crucial to determine if this swelling could be related; have you had any recent imaging scans or blood tests to check for recurrence or metastasis? I would also like to know if the swelling is soft and movable or if it feels hard and fixed to the underlying tissues. REQUEST TEST: Neck Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ultrasound of the Neck: Well-circumscribed lesion in the subcutaneous tissue suggestive of a cystic nature.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound suggests a benign cystic lesion, but given your history of diabetes and the location on the nape, we must rule out an abscess or hidradenitis suppurativa. Is the skin over the swelling red, warm, or tender to the touch, and do you have any draining sinus tracts or blackheads in the area?

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the ultrasound indicates a well-circumscribed cystic lesion and you have no signs of acute infection like redness or warmth, this is likely a benign epidermoid or sebaceous cyst. Do you have any personal or family history of neurofibromatosis, and does the swelling feel soft and doughy rather than firm?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Colon cancer (colectomy performed), type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, osteoarthritis of the left knee. Social history: Works as a traffic warden, frequently plays golf.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the location on the nape of the neck and the cystic nature of the lesion, I need to rule out a pilomatrixoma or a complex epidermoid cyst. Do you notice any calcification or a hard, stone-like feel within the swelling upon palpation? REQUEST TEST: CT Scan of the Neck

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the CT scan is normal and the ultrasound shows a well-circumscribed cystic lesion, this strongly points to a benign epidermoid cyst rather than a malignancy or pilomatrixoma. I will now proceed with the final assessment. DIAGNOSIS READY: Epidermoid Cyst
